title: Relative torsor extension and Ext-normalized supported cohomology
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion and $j:W=T\setminus Z\hookrightarrow T$ its open complement [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, and let $(P,s)$ be a $G$-torsor with a specified section on $W$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves, def-amb-torsor-with-section]. Use ordinary derived Ext [def-pc-ext, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Put $Q=i_*\mathbf Z_Z$ and let $p:\mathbf Z_T\to Q$ be restriction. Let $\beta(P,s)\in\operatorname{Ext}^1_T(Q,G)$ be the extension characterized by an equivariant map $P\to\mathcal E$ to the fibre over $p(1)$ which sends $s$ to zero [lem-sp-relative-torsor-extension]. Let $c(P,s)\in H^1(T,W;G)$ be the Ext-normalized relative class of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology]. Use the signed cone $C^q=I^q(T)\oplus I^{q-1}(W)$ with $D(a,b)=(da,\operatorname{res}(a)-db)$ for an injective resolution $G\to I$ [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $\Psi_G^q:\operatorname{Ext}^q_T(Q,G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(T,W;G)$ be the supported-Hom comparison of [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] for integral coefficients, normalized by the kernel inclusion $z\mapsto(z,0)$ and evaluation at $1$; identify relative and supported cohomology by [lem-pur-divisor-relative-cone]. Then
$$\Psi_G^1(\beta(P,s))=c(P,s).$$
For a morphism of such framed torsors, an etale pullback, or a restriction of $s$ to an open $W'\subseteq W$, the corresponding classes agree under the canonical coefficient, pullback, or enlargement-of-support maps. Forgetting support sends $\beta(P,s)$ to the ordinary torsor extension class: precomposition by $p$ has torsor $P$ as its fibre over $1$, with its given $G$-action. Consequently the image of $\Psi_G^1(\beta(P,s))$ in $H^1(T,G)$ is the positive ordinary torsor class of $P$ [lem-sc-torsor-h1]. No Cartier or global triviality hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Identify Hom from the supported integral constant sheaf with the supported-sections functor: integerSectionEquiv identifies maps from the constant integers with global sections, and the cokernel property of the open-closed sequence identifies the maps vanishing on the complementary open with maps from its closed quotient. Naturality makes this an additive natural isomorphism. Apply exists_ext_rightDerived_cocycle_comparison. Use the realization and kernel inclusion of relativeConeSupportComparison to obtain the normalized isomorphism to relative cohomology. Every extMk class has its canonical supported cycle; its two cone coordinates determine it, which proves uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1, relative refinement using the open-closed sequence

proof.text: Choose a representative short exact extension and framed equivariant lift. Extend the resolution augmentation across its monomorphism by injectivity. Descend its differential along the epimorphic quotient to a closed map k from the supported integers to I^1. Factor through the cycles sheaf. Naturality of extension classes for the resulting map to the first resolution row, together with extMk_firstCycles and mk₀_comp_extMk, gives I.extMk(k)=-beta. The induced map from the torsor to the lifting torsor is equivariant and kills the frame. Its relative frame cycle has global coordinate k(p(1)) and zero open coordinate. Apply the defining normalization of the comparison, then negate, to obtain Psi(beta)=-relativeTorsorEquiv.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1, relative refinement using the open-closed sequence

proof.text: For coefficient and quotient morphisms, use the universal property of the free torsor extension. Kill the lift of the frame by its cokernel. The two short exact sequences show that this cokernel is a relative extension. An equivariant framed map into any target sequence factors uniquely through that cokernel and gives a morphism of short complexes. Naturality of extension classes proves the coefficient equality. Apply normalization and relativeTorsorEquiv_coefficient for the cohomology equality.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1, relative refinement using the open-closed sequence

proof.text: Finite base change makes the closed integral exchange invertible. The mate identity for the exchange and composition coherence of constant-sheaf pullback show that it carries the pulled integral unit to the target integral unit. A pulled-frame torsor map into a target extension gives, by the preceding universal property, a morphism to its direct image. Transpose this morphism through upperStarLowerStarAdjunction. Exact inverse image preserves the source short exact sequence, and the transposed maps form a morphism of short exact sequences. Naturality and mapExactFunctor_extClass give the stated inverse-exchange Ext pullback. Normalization and relativeTorsorEquiv_transfer give the relative cohomology equality.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1, relative refinement using the open-closed sequence

proof.text: For inclusion of complementary opens, the open-closed cokernel property gives the unique supported quotient map with p prime followed by this map equal to p. Apply the framed extension morphism construction to the restriction of the same frame; its vanishing follows from naturality. Naturality of extension classes gives the enlargement equality. For relative cohomology, choose a resolution lifting presentation of the torsor and use relativeFrameClass_map_eq with identity global map, restriction on the open, and zero boundary.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1, relative refinement using the open-closed sequence

proof.text: The equivariant framed lift identifies the torsor with the lifting torsor of p(1), hence identifies each section set with the displayed fibre and preserves the given action. The ordinary free extension maps to the relative extension, by its universal property, with identity on G and p on the quotient. Naturality of extension classes identifies precomposition by p with the ordinary extension class. Finally use the negative raw normalization, relativeFrameClass_forget and classH1_lifts: the two minus signs cancel, giving the positive ordinary torsor class.
